name: Memory
description: Persistent cross-session memory plus a per-session short-term scratchpad. Saves via the inline <ma::emit::memory> tag (zero-friction, mid-response), reads/edits/removes via the MemoryTool (structured CRUD by id). Three scopes: global (~/.minimal-agent/memory.md), project (~/.minimal-agent/projects/<cwd>/memory.md), short-term (~/.minimal-agent/sessions/<sid>.scratch.md). Persistent scopes are query-only by default (`MemoryTool({action: "list"})`), while short-term rides as a per-turn user-message attachment.

tool.name: MemoryTool
tool.description: List, read, add, edit, or remove saved memories. Memories are not shown in your system prompt by default, so query them whenever a saved lesson might apply (a familiar bug symptom, the user's preferences, a prior solution in this codebase). Three scopes: `global` (about working with this user), `project` (about this codebase), `short-term` (this session only). For in-flight saves mid-response, prefer the inline <ma::emit::memory> tag (lower friction, the save-echo returns the id next turn). `list` is paginated: newest 20 entries, bodies clipped to ~160 chars, with a paste-ready `next:` hint. Use `read` for one bullet's full body by id. `id` is required for read/edit/remove, `body` for add/edit, `query`/`limit`/`offset` are list-only. `clear` is short-term only.

scope.description: Which memory file to act on.

id.description: Bullet id from a prior <memory-saved> echo, list result, or save-echo. Required for read/edit/remove. Persistent ids look like `lwq8tg-a8f3`, short-term ids are integers like `3`.

body.description: New body for add or edit. Single-line preferred, multi-line is collapsed to one line.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter for action=list. Pairs with limit/offset for filtered pagination.

limit.description: For action=list, page size. Default 20, max 100 (over-large values are clamped). Pair with `offset` to page through the full set.

offset.description: For action=list, number of entries to skip counted FROM THE NEWEST END. offset=0 (default) returns the most recent page, offset=20 returns the page before that, and so on. The response header's `next:` hint shows the exact value for the next page.

format.description: Result format. `text` (default) returns a compact human-readable list. `json` returns a structured shape suitable when you need to extract specific values.

tool.reason: tool name already includes plugin identity (Memory)
